prose_updates.tldr: For the arbitrary-horizon local subclass with at most one substantively informative continuation hazard, a finite graph-and-audit rule is necessary and sufficient for the entire endpoint intervention distribution. Empty or purely lagged hazard parents need no audit; current or lead parents require one pre-\(k\) dropout stratum to audit a coordinate at or downstream of the latest such parent. Successful passive and active branches return explicit rational reconstructions valid without rank assumptions, while failure returns a strictly positive observationally equivalent pair. The minimal frontier is the empty design in the passive case and otherwise consists of \(k(T-j_\star+1)\) singleton audits. A one-way embedded-witness obstruction applies to arbitrary local supergraphs, but sufficiency with two or more informative hazards remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published monotone-missingness m-DAG theory treats a broader graph class through recovery and obstruction results, and randomized double-sampling theory usually completes the coarsened record. Neither supplies a necessary-and-sufficient partial-audit rule for an endpoint intervention distribution even in the arbitrary-horizon local class with at most one substantively informative hazard.
project_justification.niche: The completed subclass allows the sole possibly informative hazard to have any subset of its lagged, current, and lead local parents. It covers arbitrary finite alphabets, null allowed-arrow effects, and deficient transition ranks, while retaining a graph-explicit recovery-or-positive-obstruction alternative.
project_justification.fill: Define \(J_+(S_k)=S_k\cap\{k,k+1\}\). Passive sets \(J_+(S_k)=\varnothing\) are recovered from the pre-hazard risk set and complete-case Markov tail without auditing. Otherwise, with \(j_\star=\max J_+(S_k)\), a finite scan for \(d<k\) and \(\ell\in B_d\) satisfying \(\ell\ge j_\star\) returns either a rational reconstruction or a strictly positive witness, proves \(\mathsf C_{1,\mathrm{loc}}=\operatorname{GID}\), and enumerates the complete minimal frontier.

prose_updates.related_work: Tikka and Karvanen (2025) analyze a broader monotone-missingness m-DAG class and establish recovery and nonidentification results, but do not give a necessary-and-sufficient theorem for same-subject partial-audit designs. The present theorem closes that design question only for the arbitrary-horizon local subclass with at most one substantively informative hazard; its one-parent witness also yields a necessary obstruction in larger local graphs. Tikka and Karvanen (2024) study categorical rank conditions, whereas both affirmative branches here require no transition-rank premise. Levis et al. (2024) identify smooth complete-data functionals after randomized intensive follow-up that completes the coarsened record, while the sufficient designs here can recover neither the full trajectory nor the endpoint. Guo and Nabi (2026) give a sound intervention-tree construction without the restricted-class completeness theorem proved here. Duarte et al. (2024) provide finite polynomial optimization machinery used only for projected confidence sets, not for the graph-explicit criterion.
prose_updates.interpretation: The design elbow is exact in the completed subclass. If the sole possibly informative hazard depends only on the preceding state, routine observation through visit \(k-1\) supplies its unbiased mixing distribution and complete cases supply the conditional endpoint tail, so no audit is needed. If it depends on the current or next state, one audit before hazard \(k\) must reveal a state no earlier than the latest such parent; any one such incidence suffices, and without it a positive scaling cancellation changes the intervention endpoint while preserving every observed pattern table.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Constructive sufficiency is proved only when all substantively informative response dependence is confined to one hazard, although that hazard may use any subset of its lagged, current, and lead local parents. The embedded witness gives a necessary condition for arbitrary local supergraphs, not a sufficient one. Two or more informative hazards can create interacting selection factors, overlapping-parent constraints, alphabet-sensitive bridges, endpoint-only cancellations, and positive countermodel-gluing problems not resolved by the present scan. No efficiency, covariance nonsingularity, polynomial-time, or fixed-rank negative conclusion is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The field claim is an arbitrary-horizon necessary-and-sufficient design theorem for the full at-most-one-informative-hazard local subclass: \(S_t=\varnothing\) for \(t\ne k\) and \(S_k\subseteq\{k-1,k,k+1\}\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}\). It covers empty, lagged, current, lead, and combined parents; every specified finite alphabet with at least two states per visit; every positive substantive and response law; null effects on allowed arrows; and deficient transition ranks. It supplies an evaluable reconstruction, a legal positive countermodel on failure, and the exact minimal frontier. For arbitrary local graphs it supplies only the one-way active-parent obstruction, and it makes no sufficiency claim with two or more informative hazards. No shadow-variable rank, parametric selection, missing-at-random, or faithfulness assumption is imposed.
